Hi Erin — thanks for the clear ask and the samples. I sketched a compact savings model and a recommended pilot/commit structure (attached). High level summary here so you can share with procurement quickly: 

1) Expected savings for your profile (median seq 80, peak QPS 60):
   - Safe quantization (per-channel int8 + calibration): ~1.6x token cost reduction vs fp16 for GPU inference in our hosted tier; typical accuracy delta <1% on intent-classification/chat quality for the open-arch model we demoed.
   - Aggressive path (mixed int4 on non-critical layers + int8 on attention): up to ~2.2x cost reduction but requires QA on a representative eval set (we recommend running this in a short controlled pilot).
   - Batching + continuous batching: for your peak patterns we estimate 20–35% effective cost reduction when latency SLO is 200ms p95 (larger gains if you accept relaxed p95).
   - Prefix/KV cache for repeated system prompts: can cut token generation cost by an additional ~10–25% depending on prompt reuse.

2) Packaging suggestion for a 6-month PoV:
   - 6-week technical pilot (no commit): includes 50k inference credits and one quantization assessment with our SEs.
   - Follow-on ramp band (month 2–6): 3-tier commit bands with escalating discounts: 10% for $10k/mo committed usage, 18% for $25k/mo, 25% for $50k/mo. (Exact numbers in draft MAP attached).
   - We can include automated batching/caching tuning from Redwood Optimize as part of the pilot to validate savings.

I attached a short spreadsheet (edgefin_savings_model.xlsx) with the assumptions; Aditya added the rapid quant guidance in the PDF.

Next steps: I recommend a quick sync with Procurement + your engineering lead so Aditya can confirm accuracy targets for the conservative vs aggressive quant paths. Vivek — are we able to firm up the pilot credits on our side?

Thanks,
Jasmine

Erin — quick technical note from the SE side to help Procurement assess risk tradeoffs. TL;DR: start with per-channel int8 + calibration, then evaluate mixed int4 where accuracy meets your threshold.

Details (short):
- Model: the catalog model we demoed (ref: redwood-m-1) is robust to per-channel symmetric int8 post-training quantization with minimal retraining. We recommend using KL-divergence calibration on a 5–10k prompt sample for best layer-wise scaling.
- Accuracy checks: run the 1k-sample A/B pass we included in the sheet; look at intent recall and token-level perplexity delta — if intent recall drop <0.8% and top-1 response BLEU/ROUGE delta small, proceed.
- Latency: int8 yields slightly lower peformance vs fp16 for very short sequences because kernel overhead dominates; batching (N>4) flips the math and int8 becomes strictly cheaper while staying within 200ms p95 in our benchmarks.
- Operational caveats: int4 mixed configs have higher variance across outlier inputs (long-form generations) — fallback routing to fp16 or int8 is recommended for outliers. Redwood can configure automatic fallback rules in the pilot.

If you want, we can run a short 48–72 hour quant trial against a shadow copy of your eval set as part of the technical pilot.

—Aditya

Erin — happy to propose an economic structure that gets Procurement comfortable while keeping the pilot meaningful. Quick offer:

1) Technical pilot (6 weeks):
   - No commitment, includes 50k credits (applies to both hosted inference tokens and Optimize advisory hours).
   - One quantization assessment (Aditya leads), one optimizer tuning pass, and a joint savings readout at pilot close.
2) If EdgeFin converts to a 6-month committed band within 30 days of pilot close:
   - Tier A: $10k/mo commit -> 10% discount (annual-equivalent rate applied monthly).
   - Tier B: $25k/mo commit -> 18% discount + 10k one-time onboarding credits.
   - Tier C: $50k/mo commit -> 25% discount + 25k onboarding credits + a dedicated SLA addendum.
3) Trade-offs & guardrails:
   - We will set measurable targets in the MAP: pilot must show >=1.6x unit-cost reduction (conservative int8 + batching) to trigger Tier B fast-track.
   - For aggressive quantization (int4), we include a short productionization checklist and a 30-day QA rollback window.

Lauren — I've penciled the onboarding credits against our pilot budget. Can you confirm?

Erin — if this looks close, I'll draft a short MAP doc and we can route it to Procurement.

Thanks,
Vivek
